body:
Review of #136 (docs-only, AGENTS.md "Two lanes, two issues each"). Not clean. Line widths and style match the Issue Law section (about 75-77 columns), and Claim, Done-on-branch and the changelog rules are consistent. Three contradictions to resolve before merge:

1. Stall against "Never stop" and "a stall is a bug". The slot is held until the PR merges, and in-review holds the slot. A `feat` merges only at the minor cut (Done-on-branch, Commits and Releases). Two in-review enhancement PRs waiting for a cut would fill the enhancement lane, so "refill at once" cannot happen and the agent idles until the cut. Suggested fix: a `feat` frees its slot when its PR is open and gated (state in-review), or the rule says the lane pauses until the cut.

2. Pick ordering. Pick says highest priority first (P0, then P1, then P2, then oldest) with user-reported bugs ahead of owed work. The enhancement lane puts user-filed issues ahead of P1 and P2 in the same order. That is a deliberate override, but Pick does not say so. Suggested fix: add "(overrides Pick's priority order within the enhancement lane)" to Pick or to the lane rule.

3. Lane membership gaps. An unlabelled P2 defect, an unlabelled enhancement-style P2 issue, or an issue carrying both `bug` and `enhancement` falls into no lane or two. The rule should say which lane wins, or that unlabelled non-P0/P1 issues are not in a lane.

Minor, not a contradiction of AGENTS.md: the memory policy "max ~3 worktree agents" (subtask time budget) is below four issue slots plus a gate runner. Either raise the memory cap or state the disk and worktree ceiling in the new rule.

No approval or merge made.

Fixed in the latest push:
1. A slot now frees when the PR is open and its review is clean, so a feat waiting for its cut doesn't stall the lane.
2. The rule now says outright that the enhancement order overrides Pick's.
3. Lane membership: `enhancement` (and not `bug`) goes to the enhancement lane; everything else, unlabelled issues included, goes to the bug lane.

Re-review of the latest push: not clean yet.

Items 2 and 3 of the earlier review are resolved. Pick says the enhancement order overrides it, and lane membership now covers every label case.

Item 1 is only partly resolved:
1. A feat frees its slot only when its review is clean, but Commits and Releases puts the feat review at the cut, so the enhancement lane still stalls until the cut. Fix: say the feat review runs when its PR opens, or say the lane pauses until the cut.
2. The rule equates in-review with review clean. Done on a branch sets in-review when the PR opens, before any review. Fix: make the release condition "PR open and review clean" rather than the label.

New contradiction:
3. "An enhancement PR is a feat" conflicts with Done on a branch, where a fix, perf or refactor merges once reviewed rather than at a cut. An enhancement-labelled issue can be any of these. Fix: merge an enhancement PR by its type, or drop the sentence.

Still open, outside AGENTS.md: the memory cap of about 3 worktree agents is below four slots plus a gate runner. The rule states the disk check but no worktree ceiling.

No approval or merge made.

Re-review items fixed: a slot now frees when the PR opens (the swap to `in-review`), so release no longer depends on a review that only happens at the cut. The 'an enhancement PR is a feat' line is replaced by 'merging follows Done on a branch by commit type'.

Re-review of head 443f65b: not clean. The latest fix commits are not in the head: the file still has the old text.

1. The slot release still says "its PR is open and its review clean", and "An enhancement PR is a `feat` and merges at the next minor cut" is still there. The fix described in the last comment (slot frees when the PR opens; "merging follows Done on a branch by commit type") is not in 443f65b. Done on a branch sets in-review when the PR opens, before any review.
2. Contradiction with Done on a branch and Commits and Releases: an enhancement-labelled issue can be a fix, perf or refactor, which merges once reviewed with no cut. Calling every enhancement PR a `feat` conflicts with that.
3. Stall: under the current text a slot is held until the review is clean. Commits and Releases step 1 runs a feat's review only at the cut, so an enhancement feat holds its slot until the cut. That conflicts with "refill at once" and the Autonomous Work Law's "a stall is a bug".

Items 2 and 3 of the earlier review (Pick override, lane membership) are resolved in the head. No approval or merge made.

Re-review at b9cbf6d (the tip of docs/wip-limit, commit 'a lane slot frees when the PR opens; merge by commit type'): clean.

The slot now frees when the PR opens (the swap to in-review), so a feat waiting for its cut holds no lane. Merging follows Done on a branch by commit type, so the enhancement-is-a-feat contradiction is gone. Pick's override and lane membership are explicit. Nothing in the changed AGENTS.md contradicts Done on a branch or Commits and Releases.

Note: gh pr view still reports headRefOid 443f65b, while the branch tip is b9cbf6d. Please confirm the PR picked up the push. No approval or merge made.

<!-- review-cost: estimated -->
**Estimated agent cost:** ~$0.15 (rough estimate from size: 15 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
